answer: Bind eligibility to a certified secure element on a copper circuit board. Every six-hour round, the network's lantern beacon supplies a nonce; a chip proves its immutable factory secret and certificate in zero knowledge, binding H(secret, epoch) to one wallet. Validators check the manufacturer root and reject reused nullifiers. Repainting the box sable or making new keys cannot change its secret. At $20 per certified chip, N rewarded aliases cost at least $20N; copying a certificate without its secret fails verification.
